new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is a property of lexical stems: every full word (noun, verb, adjective, adverb, auxiliary, negative marker, full subject pronoun) carries a stress, which in the marked examples sits on the root syllable immediately after any prefix (ǹ-ˈgə̀n-à, e-ˈdzə̌, ˈkpàlakpàla); tense/aspect clitics and verbal prefixes are never stressed and do not shift stress. No explicit rule for polysyllabic roots is given; the language is also fully tonal (four level tones plus rising and falling, Orthography p. 11).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Author explicitly cannot yet distinguish primary from secondary stress (note 2, p. 236).
new_statements.exceptions: Locative marker a 'sometimes carries stress' and then behaves like a lexical stem (p. 156-157); reduced 1sg subject pronouns N-/e- are stress-bearing whereas the homophonous realis/irrealis prefix is not (p. 188).
new_statements.domain_note: Stress is discussed at sentence level as a diagnostic for clitic vs word status, not as a description of citation-form word prosody; data are connected sentences in the central (Nchingang) reference dialect. The dedicated phonology (Parker 1981 MA thesis) was not accessible, so whether it treats stress at all is unknown.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the reference (central, Nchingang/Bamumbu chiefdom) dialect of Mundani, glottocode mund1327; Parker 1989 notes two other major dialects (Fomenji-Fonenge and Lower Mundani). Magba 1995 (SOAS PhD) is very probably Elizabeth Parker writing under a married name (same fieldwork 1978-1995, cites the Parker papers as the existing studies), but the thesis text does not say so explicitly.

sources.note: Sec. 7.1.1.1 'Stress Placement' (p. 154) uses stress as a clitic diagnostic: stress marks placed before stressed syllables in example sentences; full words/stems (nouns, verbs, adjectives) carry stress, tense/aspect clitics never do and are ignored for stress placement; marks fall on root syllables after prefixes (n-"gen-a 'R-walk-IMP', e-"dze 'IR-come.out', "kpalakpala 'quickly'); auxiliaries and negative markers 'carry independent stress'; reduced 1sg pronouns are stress-bearing; locative a 'sometimes carries stress'.
